back_translation: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years draw near when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them.”
Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain.
In that day the keepers of the house will tremble, the strong men will stoop, the grinding women will cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows will grow dim.
The double doors to the street will be shut as the sound of the mill fades; one will rise at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song will grow faint.

People will be afraid of heights, and terrors will be along the road; the almond tree will blossom, the grasshopper will drag itself along heavily, and the caper berry will fail — for man is going to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the streets.
Before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is broken, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel broken down at the well.
Then the dust will return to the earth as it once was, and the spirit will return to God who gave it.
“Utterly without substance,” says the Teacher. “Everything is without substance.”
Moreover, besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
The Teacher sought to find delightful words, and what was written was upright — words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads, and the collected sayings are like firmly driven nails, given by the one Shepherd.
My child, beyond these, be warned: of the making of many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.
When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, together with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
